name: Benaiah
overview: Benaiah was a male descendant of Parosh noted for having married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:25. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His mention highlights a specific family circumstance during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Benaiah means 'YHWH has built,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to God's providence. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a significant reminder of divine construction or establishment.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Benaiah as a descendant of Parosh according to Ezra 10:25. Beyond this lineage, no other family relationships are recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Benaiah’s significance lies in his mention as part of the community reforms after the exile, specifically in the context of intermarriage with foreign wives. This detail underscores the challenges faced by Israel in maintaining covenantal purity and obedience to God’s commands during the restoration period. His inclusion in Ezra highlights the communal efforts to address these issues under divine guidance.
